newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan airports privatisation seen by 2000 - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Milan airports privatisation seen by 2000 - Salomon.

text.p: Milan's two airports Linate and Malpensa are seen moving towards privatisation with a public offering by the end of the decade, according to a research note on European Airports by brokers Salomon Brothers.

Milan airports are operated by Societa Escercizi Aeroportuali SpA (SEA), with public shareholders owning 99.96 percent. The main public shareholders are the Municipality of Milan which owns 84.6 percent and the Province of Milan 14.5 percent, with private shareholder 0.04 percent.

"Management believe that conditions are right for the Municipality of Milan to make a public offering of Milan airports, and it is widely believed that some form of privatisation will take place by the year 2000," said the report's author Salomon analyst Arend Dikkers.
Linate is 10 km east of Milan's centre and is used for short haul flights, but it has reached capacity, has no space to expand and can not handle large wide-bodied aircraft.
Malpensa is 45 km north-west of Milan, and a 2 trillion lire capital improvement programme is currently under way to consolidate all international and most domestic operations at the airport.

The so-called Malpensa 2000 project is to double the runway capacity, build a new terminal, expand apron and cargo areas and other facilities. Planned capacity for the airport is 24 million passengers annually, or nearly five times current capacity.

On completion of the first phase of the project, SEA will transfer all international and some domestic traffic to Malpensa from Linate, leaving only a Milan-Rome shuttle service at Linate. As a result capacity at Linate will be reduced to six million passengers from the current ten million.
Malpensa will then take 80 percent of Milan air passenger traffic and 90 percent of cargo.

"By 1998, the first phase of the Malpensa 2000 capital improvement programme will be completed. Sale of some or all of its stake in SEA would provide the City with a significant opportunity to generate cash for reinvestment into the airport system or for other purposes," Dikkers said.
Railway connections are under construction between Malpensa and Milan's centre, and major improvement to the road system to the airport is also underway.
SEA made an operating profit of 126 billion lire and a net profit of 52 billion lire in 1995.
The report entitled "European Airports - Destination Private Sector" initiates coverage of the European Airport Industry by Salomon Brothers.
